blocks.x: Cyber & Zero-Trust inside Agriculture & Food Systems: what the sector's controls demand, what we build on the platform rails, and the outcomes written into the engagement.

In Agriculture & Food Systems, cybersecurity & zero-trust covers architecture-level security programs: zero-trust network and workload design, identity modernization, threat intelligence and managed detection, cloud posture management, ai-specific security for models and agents, cyber resilience, and the compliance machinery (soc 2, iso 27001, pci dss, dora) that regulated industries must evidence. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: zero-trust architecture & implementation, threat intelligence & managed soc, identity & access modernization — delivered on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Agronomic decisions run on tradition because soil, weather and crop telemetry are patchy; input spend is uniform where it should be variable.
Origin, organic and deforestation-free claims face EUDR-grade scrutiny; evidence is paper and trust.
Harvest forecasting is regional guesswork; quality attributes (protein, moisture, defects) are discovered at intake, not predicted.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The pattern pulls 7 services from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower (Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation, Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC, Identity & Access Modernization, Cloud Security & Posture Management form the usual core) and sequences them through the Dataq Method; EUDR obligations shape the design from sprint one.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Never trust, always verify: zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Detection that keeps pace: intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.
Identity as the perimeter: workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
Secure at the control plane: posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
Subsidy/loan application verification with cross-source analytics (fraud and error capture up)
Segmentation for farm/processing OT and office estates (ransomware exposure reduced)

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: EUDR and Food-safety regimes (HACCP/EU 178/FSMA). Traceability and recall duties. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Below is the delivery cadence for this capability — the same pattern on every engagement. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline with your team: the current metric is measured, signed and stored as the reference for every later gate. Weeks 3–8 run the pilot on deliberately narrow scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, never quietly extended.
